question: What is the primary purpose of inflammation in the human body?

options.A: To decrease blood flow to injured areas
options.B: To permanently increase the body temperature
options.C: To speed up the breakdown of red blood cells
options.D: To destroy foreign invaders and repair damaged tissue

explanation: The immune system initiates inflammation specifically to neutralize threats and heal injuries. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why would a person die from a minor infection if they had no inflammatory response?

options.A: The liver would immediately stop producing essential proteins
options.B: Blood pressure would drop too low to sustain life
options.C: The body could not isolate and destroy invading germs
options.D: Red blood cells would stop carrying oxygen to tissues

explanation: Inflammation is the critical defense mechanism that walls off and eliminates harmful agents in the body. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which type of white blood cell is most dominant in acute inflammation?
explanation: Neutrophils are the first responders that rush to the site of an acute injury. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h2)

question: A patient has had lingering joint swelling for over eight months. What type of inflammation is this?
explanation: You got it! When inflammation hangs around for months with continuous immune activity, we call it chronic.

question: Which classic Latin term describes the redness seen during acute inflammation?
explanation: Correct! 'Rubor' is the medical term for redness caused by extra blood rushing to an inflamed area. Think 'ruby red'!

question: What directly causes pain (dolor) during an acute inflammation?

options.A: Rapid freezing of the skin cells surrounding the wound
options.B: Complete lack of oxygen in the local muscle tissue
options.C: Direct destruction of the spinal cord by white blood cells
options.D: Pressure from swelling and chemicals irritating nerve endings

explanation: Spot on! The swelling stretches local tissues and triggers chemical signals that wake up nearby pain receptors.

question: What is the term for white blood cells squeezing through tiny blood vessel walls into injured tissue?
explanation: Great job! Diapedesis is just the clever way white blood cells slip out of the bloodstream to join the fight at the tissue level.

question: Why do blood vessels become more permeable during the early stages of acute inflammation?

options.A: To allow protective fluid and white blood cells to enter the tissue
options.B: To cause immediate clotting and seal off the skin surface
options.C: To flush harmful bacteria directly back into the major arteries
options.D: To prevent any blood from reaching the injured site

explanation: Increased permeability lets immune cells and proteins escape the bloodstream to fight the infection at the tissue level. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which blood test measures how fast red blood cells settle to check for inflammation?
explanation: Spot on! The ESR test checks how fast red blood cells clump and fall to the bottom; inflammation makes them drop faster.

question: What does a 'shift to the left' on a white blood cell differential usually indicate?

options.A: A complete absence of red blood cells in the circulating blood
options.B: An increased release of immature neutrophils from the bone marrow
options.C: Normal recovery and healing of chronic scar tissue
options.D: An allergic reaction caused by environmental pollen

explanation: When acute demand for infection-fighting cells is high, the bone marrow pumps out immature neutrophils, known as a left shift. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h5)

question: Which vital sign change usually comes with a widespread inflammatory response?
explanation: Correct! Fever is a classic full-body response triggered when inflammatory signals talk to the brain's temperature control center.

question: A nurse is caring for a patient with a surgical wound. Which finding suggests the local inflammation is worsening into a serious infection?

options.A: A slight drop in blood pressure after getting out of bed
options.B: Mild itching directly over the healing scar line
options.C: Normal skin color surrounding the closed surgical staples
options.D: Pus drainage and spreading redness around the incision

explanation: Purulent drainage and expanding erythema are classic clinical indicators of worsening infection in a wound. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h6)

question: How do non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) help relieve pain?

options.A: Blocking prostaglandins to reduce pain and swelling
options.B: Destroying bacteria directly in the bloodstream
options.C: Permanently stopping all white blood cell production
options.D: Freezing the skin to numb local nerve endings

explanation: You nailed it! NSAIDs stop the body from making prostaglandins, which are the chemical messengers of pain and swelling.

question: Why is cold therapy (ice) applied during the first 24 to 48 hours following an acute soft tissue injury?

options.A: It increases blood flow to warm up the injured muscle
options.B: It causes vasoconstriction to reduce local swelling and pain
options.C: It forces white blood cells to leave the body entirely
options.D: It stimulates scar tissue to form much faster

explanation: Cold constricts local blood vessels, decreasing the amount of fluid that leaks into the surrounding injured tissue. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h7)

question: What is a major long-term risk of persistent, chronic inflammation in the body?

options.A: Rapid and permanent healing of all damaged joints
options.B: Progressive tissue destruction and organ dysfunction
options.C: Complete prevention of future bacterial infections
options.D: Immediate disappearance of all white blood cells

explanation: Chronic inflammation causes ongoing immune activity that slowly breaks down healthy tissue and impairs organ function. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h8)

question: Which of these habits will NOT help reduce overall inflammation in the body?
explanation: Correct! Smoking actually ramps up inflammation and oxidative stress, whereas healthy eating, exercise, and stress control calm it down.
